findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission error, or unreadable path causes unhandled panic instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV field (non-numeric, empty, or out-of-range for u32) aborts the entire function instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Parse into u16 directly with .parse::<u16>() and propagate via map_err or ?; never unwrap user-derived input

findings.problem: Lossy cast from u32 to u16 via .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16, corrupting data without any error indication
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>() so out-of-range values are rejected by the parser; use u16::try_from if a u32 source is unavoidable

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() followed by indexed access parts[0], parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: Collects all CSV parts into a Vec<String> unnecessarily; split + collect is overkill when only two fields are needed, and indexing later is unsafe
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract exactly the first and second fields, then process each branch with get/ok() for bounds safety

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] with no bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: If the CSV line has fewer than 2 fields, split + collect yields fewer parts and parts[0] or parts[1] panics at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the Some/None case, or use parts.get(0) with proper error handling

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[1] with no bounds validation
findings.failure_mode: Lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields cause a panic when accessing parts[1]
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the missing second field with None/Err rather than indexing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) mixes logging into data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: Side-effecting log call embedded in the data transformation pipeline makes the parsing logic non-deterministic and couples output to parsing
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing pipeline; if logging is needed, emit it in the shell layer after Record construction with a separate log call

findings.problem: Function load_leases mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing and domain construction
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation without mocking the filesystem; the function does too much and the pure core is not separable
findings.fix: Split into a pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and a shell fn load_leases(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that calls parse_record on each line

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to measure load_leases performance
findings.failure_mode: Allocation patterns (Vec<String> per line, collect, clone) are unmeasured; if throughput is important, the cost of per-line allocation is unknown
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similar benchmark for load_leases with representative lease file sizes

findings.problem: Per-line allocation of Vec<String> via split + map + collect with no measured budget
findings.failure_mode: Each line allocates a Vec of Strings and clones strings into Record fields; for large files this generates excessive heap traffic with no measured guard
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and borrow &str fields where possible; defer String allocation to only where owned data is required

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, cargo-flamegraph) for load_leases hot path
findings.failure_mode: Allocation-heavy parsing loop may be a hotspot with no empirical evidence to guide optimization
findings.fix: Run cargo-flamegraph or equivalent on load_leases with a representative input to identify hotspots

findings.failure_mode: No behavioral contract exists to verify correctness; parsing edge cases (empty lines, missing fields, invalid numbers) are untested
findings.fix: Add behavior tests covering: valid records, empty file, malformed lines, missing fields, out-of-range values, and invalid parse input
